records.source: הַדָּבָ֛ר אֲשֶׁר־הָיָ֥ה אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה בִּימֵ֨י יְהוֹיָקִ֧ים בֶּן־יֹאשִׁיָּ֛הוּ מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: The word which came to Jeremiah from with Yahweh in [the] days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, saying:
pieces: This message came to Jeremiah from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} during the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:

L.1: The word that came to Jeremiah from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, saying:

R.1: This is the message {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Jeremiah while Jehoiakim son of Josiah was king of Judah:

decisions.choice: in the days of Jehoiakim: some years before the events of chapter 34, which are dated to Zedekiah's reign
decisions.reason: Jehoiakim reigned about 609-598 BC (2 Kings 23:36). Verse 11 places this scene after Nebuchadrezzar's army had come against the land, most likely in the last years of Jehoiakim, when raiding bands of Chaldeans and Arameans were sent against Judah (2 Kings 24:1-2). The book sets this chapter beside chapter 34 by its theme: the Rechabites keep their word, while the people of Jerusalem broke the covenant to free their slaves (34:8-22).

decisions.choice: chapter 35 of the Hebrew is chapter 42 of the Greek translation
decisions.reason: Because the Greek translation (the Septuagint) places the oracles against the nations after 25:13, this chapter stands later there (see 1:1). The Hebrew is followed.

decisions.choice: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying: (L); This message came to Jeremiah from the LORD during the reign of (B); This is the message the LORD gave Jeremiah while ... was king (R)
decisions.reason: The heading is worded as it is set for Jeremiah (11:1; 21:1), with the date added.

records.heading: The Rechabites keep their ancestor's command

records.source: הָלוֹךְ֮ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית הָרֵכָבִים֒ וְדִבַּרְתָּ֣ אוֹתָ֔ם וַהֲבִֽאוֹתָם֙ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־אַחַ֖ת הַלְּשָׁכ֑וֹת וְהִשְׁקִיתָ֥ אוֹתָ֖ם יָֽיִן׃
records.gloss: Go to [the] house of the Rechabites and you will speak with them, and you will bring them [to the] house of Yahweh, into one of the chambers, and you will give them to drink wine.
pieces: "Go to the family of the Rechabites and speak with them. Bring them to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, into one of the side rooms, and give them wine to drink."

L.2: "Go to the house of the Rechabites and speak with them, and bring them [to] the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, into one of the chambers, and give them wine to drink."

R.2: "Go to the Rechabite family and talk with them. Bring them into one of the rooms at {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple, and offer them wine to drink."

decisions.choice: the house of the Rechabites: the clan descended from Jonadab son of Rechab, who lived by his rule
decisions.reason: The Rechabites were a family group who kept the way of life their ancestor Jonadab laid down: no wine, no houses, no farming, living in tents (verses 6-7). Jonadab, called Jehonadab in 2 Kings 10:15-23, rode with Jehu when he wiped out the worship of Baal in Israel, more than two hundred years before Jeremiah. 1 Chronicles 2:55 links the house of Rechab with the Kenites, the people of Moses' father-in-law (Judges 1:16).

decisions.choice: the chambers: rooms built around the temple courts
decisions.reason: The temple courts were lined with rooms used for storing offerings and supplies, for priests and Levites on duty, and for officials (1 Chronicles 9:26-27; Nehemiah 13:4-5). Baruch later reads Jeremiah's scroll in one of them (36:10).

decisions.choice: give them wine to drink: offer it, as a host does, in a public and holy place
decisions.reason: The verb means to give someone a drink. God does not intend the Rechabites to break their rule; verses 13-16 show the offer is a test whose refusal becomes a lesson for Judah.

decisions.choice: the family of the Rechabites (B); the Rechabite family (R)
decisions.reason: "House" here means a family line, not a building; the Rechabites had no houses (verse 7). Literal keeps "house".

records.source: וָאֶקַּ֞ח אֶת־יַאֲזַנְיָ֤ה בֶֽן־יִרְמְיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן־חֲבַצִּנְיָ֔ה וְאֶת־אֶחָ֖יו וְאֶת־כָּל־בָּנָ֑יו וְאֵ֖ת כָּל־בֵּ֥ית הָרֵכָבִֽים׃
records.gloss: And I took Jaazaniah son of Jeremiah son of Habazziniah, and his brothers and all his sons and all [the] house of the Rechabites.
pieces: So I took Jaazaniah son of Jeremiah, son of Habazziniah, with his brothers and all his sons, the whole family of the Rechabites.

L.3: So I took Jaazaniah son of Jeremiah son of Habazziniah, and his brothers and all his sons, and the whole house of the Rechabites.

R.3: So I went and brought Jaazaniah son of Jeremiah and grandson of Habazziniah, together with his brothers and all his sons. These were all the men of the Rechabite family.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah here: Jaazaniah's father, a different man from the prophet
decisions.reason: Jeremiah was a common name; another Jeremiah, of Libnah, was the father of King Jehoahaz's mother (2 Kings 23:31). Jaazaniah is the head of the Rechabites, and the prophet now tells the story himself ("I took").

decisions.choice: the whole house of the Rechabites: summing up the men just named
decisions.reason: The last phrase gathers up Jaazaniah, his brothers and his sons as the whole clan. Verse 5 speaks of the men of the house of the Rechabites being given wine.

decisions.choice: grandson of Habazziniah; These were all the men of the Rechabite family
decisions.reason: Readable says that the second "son of" names a grandfather, and makes the summing up of the last phrase its own sentence.

records.source: וָאָבִ֤א אֹתָם֙ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־לִשְׁכַּ֗ת בְּנֵ֛י חָנָ֥ן בֶּן־יִגְדַּלְיָ֖הוּ אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים אֲשֶׁר־אֵ֨צֶל֙ לִשְׁכַּ֣ת הַשָּׂרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר מִמַּ֗עַל לְלִשְׁכַּ֛ת מַעֲשֵׂיָ֥הוּ בֶן־שַׁלֻּ֖ם שֹׁמֵ֥ר הַסַּֽף׃
records.gloss: And I brought them [to the] house of Yahweh, into [the] chamber of [the] sons of Hanan son of Igdaliah, [the] man of the God, which [was] beside [the] chamber of the princes, which [was] above [the] chamber of Maaseiah son of Shallum, keeper of the threshold.
pieces: I brought them into the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to the room of the sons of Hanan son of Igdaliah, the man of God. It was next to the officials' room, above the room of Maaseiah son of Shallum, the doorkeeper.

L.4: And I brought them [into] the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, into the chamber of the sons of Hanan son of Igdaliah, the man of God, which [was] beside the chamber of the princes, which [was] above the chamber of Maaseiah son of Shallum, the keeper of the threshold.

R.4: I brought them into {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple, to the room that belonged to the sons of Hanan son of Igdaliah, the man of God. It was next to the room of the leaders, and above the room of Maaseiah son of Shallum, one of the men who guarded the temple entrance.

decisions.choice: the sons of Hanan ... the man of God: either his descendants or the followers he taught
decisions.reason: "Man of God" is a title for a prophet (1 Samuel 9:6; 1 Kings 17:18). "Sons" can mean the members of a prophet's circle, as in "the sons of the prophets" (2 Kings 2:3), as well as his children. Either way, the room was held by people friendly to a prophet, a safe place for Jeremiah to bring his guests.

decisions.choice: keeper of the threshold: one of the senior temple officers in charge of the entrances
decisions.reason: The keepers of the threshold were high temple officials; three of them were taken with the chief priest when Jerusalem fell (2 Kings 25:18; Jeremiah 52:24). Their duties included guarding the doors and receiving the money brought in (2 Kings 12:10).

decisions.choice: the chamber of the princes: the room used by the royal officials
decisions.reason: The officials of the king's court had their own room in the temple area. The scene takes place among the leaders of Judah, who would see the test.

decisions.choice: princes (L), officials (B), leaders (R); keeper of the threshold (L), doorkeeper (B), one of the men who guarded the temple entrance (R)
decisions.reason: The terms follow the wording set for these books for *sar* and for this office (2 Kings 25:18).

decisions.choice: room (B, R); chamber (L)
decisions.reason: "Chamber" is the older English word for such a room; Balanced and Readable use the everyday word.

records.source: וָאֶתֵּ֞ן לִפְנֵ֣י׀בְּנֵ֣י בֵית־הָרֵכָבִ֗ים גְּבִעִ֛ים מְלֵאִ֥ים יַ֖יִן וְכֹס֑וֹת וָאֹמַ֥ר אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם שְׁתוּ־יָֽיִן׃
records.gloss: And I set before [the] sons of [the] house of the Rechabites bowls full [of] wine and cups, and I said to them, drink wine.
pieces: Then I set pitchers full of wine and cups before the men of the Rechabite family, and I said to them, "Drink some wine."

L.5: And I set before the sons of the house of the Rechabites bowls full of wine, and cups, and I said to them, "Drink wine."

R.5: Then I put jugs full of wine and some cups in front of the Rechabite men, and I said to them, "Have some wine."

decisions.choice: bowls ... and cups: large vessels to pour from, and cups to drink from
decisions.reason: The first word names a large bowl or jar (it is used of the cups on the lampstand in Exodus 25:31-34, and of Joseph's silver cup in Genesis 44:2). Set beside "cups", it is the vessel the wine is poured from.

decisions.choice: Drink wine: a plain invitation, given openly by a prophet in the temple
decisions.reason: The prophet's command is short and direct. The setting gave every reason to accept: a prophet's offer, in the house of the LORD, with the officials nearby.

decisions.choice: pitchers (B), jugs (R); the men of (B, R) for "the sons of"
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the vessels by their use, and say "men" for "sons of the house", the members of the family present.

records.source: וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ לֹ֣א נִשְׁתֶּה־יָּ֑יִן כִּי֩ יוֹנָדָ֨ב בֶּן־רֵכָ֜ב אָבִ֗ינוּ צִוָּ֤ה עָלֵ֨ינוּ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֧א תִשְׁתּוּ־יַ֛יִן אַתֶּ֥ם וּבְנֵיכֶ֖ם עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: And they said, not we will drink wine, for Jonadab son of Rechab our father commanded on us, saying, not you will drink wine, you and your sons, until forever.
pieces: But they answered, "We do not drink wine, because our ancestor Jonadab son of Rechab commanded us, 'You must never drink wine, neither you nor your descendants.

L.6: But they said, "We will not drink wine, for Jonadab son of Rechab, our father, commanded us, saying, 'You shall not drink wine, you or your {{gender:children|sons}}, forever.

R.6: But they said, "We do not drink wine. Our ancestor Jonadab son of Rechab gave us this command: 'You must never drink wine, and your children must never drink it either.

decisions.choice: Jonadab son of Rechab: the Jehonadab of 2 Kings 10:15-23
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses the short form of the name here and in verses 10 and 19, and the long form, Jehonadab, in verses 8, 14, 16 and 18. Both are the same man, who joined Jehu against the worship of Baal (2 Kings 10:15-23). Each verse keeps the form its Hebrew uses.

decisions.choice: our father: our ancestor, the founder of the family
decisions.reason: The word for "father" also means a forefather. Jonadab lived more than two centuries earlier, so the Rechabites mean the one who founded their way of life.

decisions.choice: no wine, forever: a family vow kept as a mark of loyalty
decisions.reason: Jonadab's rule (verses 6-7) kept his family apart from settled farming life in the land, with its houses and vineyards. The Nazirite vow also gave up wine (Numbers 6:3), but it was for a set time; this rule was for every generation.

decisions.choice: our ancestor (B, R); your descendants (B), your children (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that "father" means ancestor here, and that "sons" means all who come after, as verse 8 includes wives and daughters.

records.source: וּבַ֣יִת לֹֽא־תִבְנ֗וּ וְזֶ֤רַע לֹֽא־תִזְרָ֨עוּ֙ וְכֶ֣רֶם לֹֽא־תִטָּ֔עוּ וְלֹ֥א יִֽהְיֶ֖ה לָכֶ֑ם כִּ֠י בָּאֳהָלִ֤ים תֵּֽשְׁבוּ֙ כָּל־יְמֵיכֶ֔ם לְמַ֨עַן תִּֽחְי֜וּ יָמִ֤ים רַבִּים֙ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י הָאֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתֶּ֖ם גָּרִ֥ים שָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: And house not you will build, and seed not you will sow, and vineyard not you will plant, and not it will be to you; for in tents you will dwell all your days, so that you may live days many on [the] face of the ground where you [are] sojourning there.
pieces: You must not build a house, sow seed or plant a vineyard; you must not own any of them. Instead, you must stay in tents all your lives, so that you may live many days in the land where you are outsiders.'

L.7: And a house you shall not build, and seed you shall not sow, and a vineyard you shall not plant, nor shall you have [one]; but in tents you shall live all your days, so that you may live many days on the face of the land where you are sojourning.'

R.7: Do not build houses. Do not plant crops or vineyards, and do not own any. Always live in tents. Then you will live a long time in the land where you live as strangers.'

decisions.choice: nor shall you have one: they may not own a house, a sown field or a vineyard even by other means
decisions.reason: The added clause closes the gap: the rule is not only against building or planting, but against owning such property at all. Verse 9 repeats it.

decisions.choice: sojourning: living in the land as resident outsiders without owning land
decisions.reason: The verb belongs with *ger*, the sojourner who lives among a people without the rights of a landowner (Leviticus 25:23). The Rechabites chose to live in Judah that way, like the patriarchs who lived in tents in the land promised to them (Genesis 23:4; Hebrews 11:9).

decisions.choice: that you may live many days on the land: a promise for keeping the father's command
decisions.reason: The words recall the promise attached to honoring father and mother, that one's days may be long on the land (Exodus 20:12; Deuteronomy 5:16). The Rechabites honor their father, and verse 19 gives them a lasting promise.

decisions.choice: sojourning (L), are outsiders (B), live as strangers (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for *ger* in these books: "foreigner" is kept for another word.

decisions.choice: Then you will live a long time
decisions.reason: Readable puts the purpose as a result in its own short sentence; the sense is the same.

records.source: וַנִּשְׁמַ֗ע בְּק֨וֹל יְהוֹנָדָ֤ב בֶּן־רֵכָב֙ אָבִ֔ינוּ לְכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֑נוּ לְבִלְתִּ֤י שְׁתֽוֹת־יַ֨יִן֙ כָּל־יָמֵ֔ינוּ אֲנַ֣חְנוּ נָשֵׁ֔ינוּ בָּנֵ֖ינוּ וּבְנֹתֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: And we have listened to [the] voice of Jehonadab son of Rechab our father in all that he commanded us, not to drink wine all our days, we, our wives, our sons and our daughters,
pieces: We have obeyed our ancestor Jehonadab son of Rechab in everything he commanded us: we do not drink wine as long as we live, neither we nor our wives, our sons or our daughters,

L.8: And we have listened to the voice of Jehonadab son of Rechab, our father, in all that he commanded us, not to drink wine all our days, we, our wives, our sons and our daughters,

R.8: We have obeyed everything our ancestor Jehonadab son of Rechab commanded us. In all our lives we have never drunk wine, and neither have our wives, our sons or our daughters.

decisions.choice: listened to the voice of: obeyed
decisions.reason: To "listen to the voice" of someone means to do what he says (Genesis 22:18; Exodus 19:5). The same verb runs through the chapter: the Rechabites listened to their ancestor, but Judah did not listen to the LORD (verses 13-18).

decisions.choice: Jehonadab: the longer form of Jonadab's name
decisions.reason: The same man as in verse 6; the Hebrew uses the full form here (see verse 6, m1).

decisions.choice: we, our wives, our sons and our daughters: the whole household keeps the rule
decisions.reason: The list shows that the rule bound the women and children of the clan as well as the men.

decisions.choice: obeyed
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom; Literal keeps "listened to the voice" so that the link with verses 13-18 can be seen.

records.source: וּלְבִלְתִּ֛י בְּנ֥וֹת בָּתִּ֖ים לְשִׁבְתֵּ֑נוּ וְכֶ֧רֶם וְשָׂדֶ֛ה וָזֶ֖רַע לֹ֥א יִֽהְיֶה־לָּֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: and not to build houses for our dwelling; and vineyard and field and seed not it [is] to us.
pieces: and not to build houses to live in. We have no vineyard, no field and no seed to sow.

L.9: and not to build houses for us to live in; and vineyard and field and seed we do not have.

R.9: We have not built houses to live in. We do not own vineyards or fields or seed for planting.

decisions.choice: and not to build houses: the list of what Jonadab commanded goes on from verse 8
decisions.reason: The verse continues the sentence begun in verse 8, then states what the family does not own: the things named in Jonadab's rule (verse 7).

decisions.choice: field and seed: farmland and grain to sow it with
decisions.reason: Without field or seed the family could not farm; they lived as herders in tents.

decisions.choice: We have not built houses
decisions.reason: Readable, which ended verse 8 with a full stop, starts a new sentence here.

records.source: וַנֵּ֖שֶׁב בָּֽאֳהָלִ֑ים וַנִּשְׁמַ֣ע וַנַּ֔עַשׂ כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֖נוּ יוֹנָדָ֥ב אָבִֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: And we have dwelt in tents, and we have listened and done according to all that commanded us Jonadab our father.
pieces: We have lived in tents and have obeyed and done everything our ancestor Jonadab commanded us.

L.10: And we have lived in tents, and we have listened and done according to all that Jonadab our father commanded us.

R.10: We have lived in tents. We have obeyed our ancestor Jonadab and done everything he told us to do.

decisions.choice: listened and done: obedience shown in practice
decisions.reason: Hearing and doing go together, as when Israel said at Sinai "we will do and we will listen" (Exodus 24:7). The Rechabites' life in tents is the proof.

decisions.choice: Jonadab: the short form of the name again, as in verse 6
decisions.reason: See verse 6, m1.

decisions.choice: our ancestor
decisions.reason: As in verse 6.

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י בַּעֲל֨וֹת נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶל֮ אֶל־הָאָרֶץ֒ וַנֹּ֗אמֶר בֹּ֚אוּ וְנָב֣וֹא יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם מִפְּנֵי֙ חֵ֣יל הַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים וּמִפְּנֵ֖י חֵ֣יל אֲרָ֑ם וַנֵּ֖שֶׁב בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃פ
records.gloss: And it was when came up Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon against the land, and we said, come and let us go [to] Jerusalem from before [the] army of the Chaldeans and from before [the] army of Aram; and we have dwelt in Jerusalem.
pieces: But when Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon invaded the land, we said, 'Come, let us go to Jerusalem to escape the army of the Chaldeans and the army of the Arameans.' That is why we are living in Jerusalem."

L.11: But when Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon came up against the land, we said, 'Come, and let us go to Jerusalem from before the army of the Chaldeans and from before the army of Aram.' So we are living in Jerusalem."

R.11: But when Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon attacked this country, we said, 'Come on, we must go to Jerusalem to get away from the armies of the Babylonians and the Arameans.' That is why we are living in Jerusalem now."

decisions.choice: Nebuchadrezzar: the form of the king's name this verse uses
decisions.reason: Jeremiah most often spells the name with an r (Nebuchadrezzar), closer to the Babylonian Nabu-kudurri-usur; the form with n (Nebuchadnezzar) appears elsewhere in the book (27:6; 28:3). Each verse keeps the form its Hebrew uses.

decisions.choice: the army of the Chaldeans and the army of Aram: the raiders sent against Judah in Jehoiakim's last years
decisions.reason: When Jehoiakim rebelled, the LORD sent against him bands of Chaldeans, Arameans, Moabites and Ammonites (2 Kings 24:1-2). Aram was the kingdom to the north centered on Damascus, then under Babylon. The Rechabites took refuge in the walled city, the one place they could be safe, without giving up their tents or their rule.

decisions.choice: so we are living in Jerusalem: this explains why tent dwellers were in the city
decisions.reason: The Rechabites answer the question their presence raises: they have not given up their way of life; the war has driven them inside the walls.

decisions.choice: the Babylonians (R) for the Chaldeans
decisions.reason: The wording set for these books: Readable names the people by their better known name.

records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to Jeremiah, saying:
pieces: Then the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Jeremiah:

L.12: And the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Jeremiah, saying:

R.12: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Jeremiah this message:

decisions.choice: the word came to Jeremiah: the story turns from the test to its meaning
decisions.reason: The narrator speaks of Jeremiah in the third person again, though verses 3-11 were told by Jeremiah himself. The message that follows explains what God meant by the test.

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, saying: (L); ... came to Jeremiah: (B); the LORD gave Jeremiah this message (R)
decisions.reason: The formula set for Jeremiah, with the prophet's name in place of "me".

records.source: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הָלֹ֤ךְ וְאָֽמַרְתָּ֙ לְאִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֔ה וּלְיֽוֹשְׁבֵ֖י יְרֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם הֲל֨וֹא תִקְח֥וּ מוּסָ֛ר לִשְׁמֹ֥עַ אֶל־דְּבָרַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh of hosts, [the] God of Israel: Go and you will say to [the] man of Judah and to [the] inhabitants of Jerusalem, not will you take correction to listen to my words? declaration of Yahweh.
pieces: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: Go and say to {{gender:the people|the men}} of Judah and to those who live in Jerusalem, 'Will you not accept correction and listen to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words? declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.13: "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the God of Israel: Go and say to {{gender:the people|the men}} of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, 'Will you not accept correction, to listen to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words? declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.13: "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Go and tell the people of Judah and everyone who lives in Jerusalem, 'Why will you not learn from this and obey what I say? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: correction: instruction that comes through discipline
decisions.reason: The word means training or discipline, the teaching a father gives a son, sometimes with punishment (Proverbs 1:8; 3:11). Jeremiah often says Judah would not accept it (2:30; 7:28; 32:33). Here the lesson is the Rechabites' example.

decisions.choice: Will you not accept correction ...?: a question that rebukes
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "you should". It points from the Rechabites, whom all could see in the temple, to the people's own refusal to listen.

decisions.choice: Go and say: Jeremiah is sent to make the scene a public lesson
decisions.reason: The message runs to the end of verse 17. Jeremiah is to speak it to the people of Judah and Jerusalem, who would have heard of the test in the temple.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD of hosts (L); The LORD of Armies says this (B); This is what the LORD of Armies says (R); declares (L, B), says (R)
decisions.reason: The formulas set for the prophets (Isaiah 1:9 and the wording for Jeremiah).

decisions.choice: the people of Judah, with "the men of Judah" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The singular "man of Judah" stands for all its people, women as well as men, as in 18:11.

records.source: הוּקַ֡ם אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֣י יְהוֹנָדָ֣ב בֶּן־רֵ֠כָב אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֨ה אֶת־בָּנָ֜יו לְבִלְתִּ֣י שְׁתֽוֹת־יַ֗יִן וְלֹ֤א שָׁתוּ֙ עַד־הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה כִּ֣י שָֽׁמְע֔וּ אֵ֖ת מִצְוַ֣ת אֲבִיהֶ֑ם וְאָ֨נֹכִ֜י דִּבַּ֤רְתִּי אֲלֵיכֶם֙ הַשְׁכֵּ֣ם וְדַבֵּ֔ר וְלֹ֥א שְׁמַעְתֶּ֖ם אֵלָֽי׃
records.gloss: It has been carried out, [the] words of Jehonadab son of Rechab which he commanded his sons, not to drink wine, and not they have drunk until the day this, for they have listened to [the] command of their father; and I, I have spoken to you, rising early and speaking, and not you have listened to me.
pieces: Jehonadab son of Rechab told his descendants not to drink wine, and his words have been kept: to this day they have not drunk it, because they obey their ancestor's command. I, however, have spoken to you again and again, and you have not listened to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.14: The words of Jehonadab son of Rechab, which he commanded his {{gender:children|sons}}, not to drink wine, have been carried out, and they have not drunk [wine] to this day, for they have listened to the command of their father. But I have spoken to you, rising early and speaking, and you have not listened to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.14: Jehonadab son of Rechab ordered his descendants not to drink wine, and they have done what he said. To this day they do not drink wine, because they obey their ancestor's command. But I have spoken to you over and over, and you have not listened to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: have been carried out: the verb stands first for weight
decisions.reason: The sentence opens with the verb, "carried out are the words", stressing that a mere man's command has been kept for generations. The same verb returns in verse 16.

decisions.choice: rising early and speaking: speaking persistently, again and again
decisions.reason: The phrase pictures someone who gets up early to do a task, and so means doing it eagerly and repeatedly. Jeremiah uses it often of God's speaking and sending prophets (7:13, 25; 25:3-4; 26:5).

decisions.choice: But I: God sets himself against Jonadab
decisions.reason: The pronoun is written out for contrast. Jonadab gave his command once and was obeyed; God spoke to his people again and again and was not.

decisions.choice: rising early and speaking (L); again and again (B); over and over (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this phrase in Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: Jehonadab ... told his descendants ...; and his words have been kept
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable start with the person and his command, then say that it was kept, since the Hebrew order would read awkwardly.

records.source: וָאֶשְׁלַ֣ח אֲלֵיכֶ֣ם אֶת־כָּל־עֲבָדַ֣י הַנְּבִאִ֣ים׀הַשְׁכֵּ֣ים וְשָׁלֹ֣חַ׀לֵאמֹ֡ר שֻׁבוּ־נָ֡א אִישׁ֩ מִדַּרְכּ֨וֹ הָרָעָ֜ה וְהֵיטִ֣יבוּ מַֽעַלְלֵיכֶ֗ם וְאַל־תֵּ֨לְכ֜וּ אַחֲרֵ֨י אֱלֹהִ֤ים אֲחֵרִים֙ לְעָבְדָ֔ם וּשְׁבוּ֙ אֶל־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥תִּי לָכֶ֖ם וְלַאֲבֹֽתֵיכֶ֑ם וְלֹ֤א הִטִּיתֶם֙ אֶֽת־אָזְנְכֶ֔ם וְלֹ֥א שְׁמַעְתֶּ֖ם אֵלָֽי׃
records.gloss: And I sent to you all my servants the prophets, rising early and sending, saying: turn please each from his way the evil, and make good your deeds, and not go after gods other to serve them, and dwell on the land which I gave to you and to your fathers; and not you inclined your ear and not you listened to me.
pieces: I sent you all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servants the prophets again and again, saying, "Turn back, every one of you, from your evil way, and make your deeds good. Do not follow other gods to serve them, and you will live in the land I gave to you and your ancestors." But you did not pay attention or listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.15: And I have sent to you all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servants the prophets, rising early and sending [them], saying, "Turn now, each one from {{gender:their|his}} evil way, and make good your deeds, and do not go after other gods to serve them, and dwell in the land that I gave to you and to your fathers." But you did not incline your ear, and you did not listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.15: I sent all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servants the prophets to you, over and over. They told you, "Each of you must stop living in your evil ways and start doing what is good. Do not follow other gods or serve them. Then you will live in the land I gave to you and to your ancestors." But you would not pay attention. You would not listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: the call of the prophets summed up: turn, do good, serve no other gods, and live in the land
decisions.reason: The same call is given in 25:4-6 and 7:3-7. Living in the land depended on loyalty to the LORD (Deuteronomy 4:40; 11:16-17). The Rechabites lived as outsiders in the land and kept it; Judah owned the land and was about to lose it.

decisions.choice: incline your ear: bend toward to listen, pay attention
decisions.reason: To turn the ear toward someone is to listen with care (7:24, 26; 25:4). Not even that much was done.

decisions.choice: and dwell in the land: the result promised if they turn
decisions.reason: The command "dwell" after the other commands states what will follow: if they turn, they will stay in the land.

decisions.choice: servants (all levels)
decisions.reason: As in 25:4 and 26:5, "my servants the prophets" keeps "servants": they are those who serve the LORD as his messengers.

decisions.choice: you will live (B); Then you will live (R); ancestors (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the command a promise (m3), as in 25:5, and say "ancestors" for "fathers".

records.source: כִּ֣י הֵקִ֗ימוּ בְּנֵי֙ יְהוֹנָדָ֣ב בֶּן־רֵכָ֔ב אֶת־מִצְוַ֥ת אֲבִיהֶ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֑ם וְהָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה לֹ֥א שָׁמְע֖וּ אֵלָֽי׃ס
records.gloss: For they have carried out, [the] sons of Jehonadab son of Rechab, [the] command of their father which he commanded them, and the people this not they have listened to me.
pieces: Yes, the descendants of Jehonadab son of Rechab have kept the command their ancestor gave them, but this people has not listened to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.16: Indeed, the {{gender:children|sons}} of Jehonadab son of Rechab have carried out the command of their father, which he commanded them, but this people has not listened to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.16: The descendants of Jehonadab son of Rechab have done what their ancestor commanded them to do. But these people have not listened to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: Indeed: the word stresses the point and sums up the contrast
decisions.reason: The small word can mean "for" or "because", but here it introduces the summing up of verses 14-15: the Rechabites obeyed, Judah did not.

decisions.choice: this people: the people of Judah, spoken of with distance
decisions.reason: God speaks of them as "this people" rather than "my people", a sign of how far they have turned from him (6:19, 21; 14:10-11).

decisions.choice: these people (R); this people (L, B)
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plural, which reads naturally for a group.

records.source: לָ֠כֵן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הִנְנִ֧י מֵבִ֣יא אֶל־יְהוּדָ֗ה וְאֶ֤ל כָּל־יֽוֹשְׁבֵי֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם אֵ֚ת כָּל־הָ֣רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם יַ֣עַן דִּבַּ֤רְתִּי אֲלֵיהֶם֙ וְלֹ֣א שָׁמֵ֔עוּ וָאֶקְרָ֥א לָהֶ֖ם וְלֹ֥א עָנֽוּ׃
records.gloss: Therefore thus says Yahweh, [the] God of hosts, [the] God of Israel: Here I [am] bringing to Judah and to all [the] inhabitants of Jerusalem all the disaster which I spoke against them, because I spoke to them and not they listened, and I called to them and not they answered.
pieces: Therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: I am about to bring on Judah and on all who live in Jerusalem all the disaster I have announced against them, because I spoke to them and they did not listen, and I called to them and they did not answer.'"

L.17: Therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of hosts, the God of Israel: Look, I am bringing on Judah and on all the inhabitants of Jerusalem all the disaster that I have spoken against them, because I spoke to them and they did not listen, and I called to them and they did not answer.'"

R.17: So this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I am going to bring on Judah and on everyone who lives in Jerusalem all the disaster I warned them about. I spoke to them, but they did not listen. I called to them, but they did not answer.'"

decisions.choice: the disaster: the ruin God has announced, the fall of Judah and Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The same word means evil and disaster (see 26:3). Their evil ways bring on them the evil, the ruin, that the prophets announced.

decisions.choice: against them ... to them: God now speaks of the people, not to them
decisions.reason: After "you" in verses 13-16, the message speaks of Judah in the third person, as a sentence passed on them. The words "I spoke ... I called ... they did not answer" repeat 7:13.

decisions.choice: Look, I am bringing: a disaster about to happen
decisions.reason: The word "look" with the participle announces something near at hand.

decisions.choice: the LORD, the God of hosts (L); the LORD God of Armies (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the Hebrew says "the LORD, God of hosts", with "God" before "hosts". The wording keeps it, with "hosts" and "Armies" as set for the prophets.

decisions.choice: announced (B); warned them about (R)
decisions.reason: "Spoke against them" means declared ahead of time; Balanced and Readable say so.

records.source: וּלְבֵ֨ית הָרֵכָבִ֜ים אָמַ֣ר יִרְמְיָ֗הוּ כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל יַ֚עַן אֲשֶׁ֣ר שְׁמַעְתֶּ֔ם עַל־מִצְוַ֖ת יְהוֹנָדָ֣ב אֲבִיכֶ֑ם וַֽתִּשְׁמְרוּ֙ אֶת־כָּל־מִצְוֺתָ֔יו וַֽתַּעֲשׂ֔וּ כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֖ה אֶתְכֶֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And to [the] house of the Rechabites said Jeremiah: thus says Yahweh of hosts, [the] God of Israel: because that you have listened to [the] command of Jehonadab your father and kept all his commands and done according to all that he commanded you,
pieces: Then Jeremiah said to the family of the Rechabites, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: Because you have obeyed the command of your ancestor Jehonadab, kept all his commands and done all that he commanded you,

L.18: And to the house of the Rechabites Jeremiah said, "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the God of Israel: Because you have listened to the command of Jehonadab your father, and kept all his commands, and done according to all that he commanded you,

R.18: Then Jeremiah said to the Rechabite family, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says: You have obeyed the command of your ancestor Jehonadab. You have kept all his commands and done everything he told you to do.

decisions.choice: Because you have listened ...: the reason for the promise of verse 19
decisions.reason: The sentence runs on into verse 19: because they obeyed, God makes them a promise.

decisions.choice: to the house of the Rechabites: a second message, for the Rechabites themselves
decisions.reason: After the word for Judah (verses 13-17), Jeremiah turns to the Rechabites. The order of the Hebrew, naming them first, marks the change of hearers.

decisions.choice: You have obeyed ... You have kept ...
decisions.reason: Readable states the reasons as plain sentences and gives the promise in verse 19 with "So".

records.source: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לֹֽא־יִכָּרֵ֨ת אִ֜ישׁ לְיוֹנָדָ֧ב בֶּן־רֵכָ֛ב עֹמֵ֥ד לְפָנַ֖י כָּל־הַיָּמִֽים׃פ
records.gloss: Therefore thus says Yahweh of hosts, [the] God of Israel: not will be cut off a man to Jonadab son of Rechab standing before me all the days.
pieces: therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: Jonadab son of Rechab will never be without a descendant to stand before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for all time."

L.19: therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the God of Israel: There shall not be cut off for Jonadab son of Rechab a man standing before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} all the days."

R.19: So this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Jonadab son of Rechab will always have a descendant to serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

decisions.choice: there shall not be cut off for Jonadab a man: Jonadab's line will never fail
decisions.reason: The same promise is made for David's line and for the Levitical priests (33:17-18; 1 Kings 2:4). Jonadab will always have a male descendant to carry on his family.

decisions.choice: standing before me: serving God
decisions.reason: To "stand before" a king or before the LORD means to wait on him as a servant does, ready to serve (1 Kings 10:8; 17:1). It is used of the priests and Levites who serve the LORD (Deuteronomy 10:8; 18:7). The Rechabites are promised a lasting place among those who serve him.

decisions.choice: all the days: always
decisions.reason: "All the days" means for all time to come.

decisions.choice: Jonadab: the short form of the name, as in verses 6 and 10
decisions.reason: See verse 6, m1.

decisions.choice: to serve me (R)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "stand before" (m2); Literal and Balanced keep the picture.
